skill.name: twscrape
skill.description: Guides safe use of twscrape for Twitter/X data collection, account setup, proxy configuration, exports, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Use twscrape to collect public Twitter/X data with async Python workflows and clear operational cautions.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: Manual review found no prompt injection, hidden code execution, or covert network exfiltration. Most static proxy, URL, file-write, and tweet-id findings are documentation examples, but local account databases and explicit rate-limit evasion guidance remain real risks.

remediation.issue: The skill promotes bypassing Twitter/X API limitations through account rotation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove bypass language and add clear lawful-use, consent, and platform-compliance boundaries for collection workflows.

remediation.issue: Examples handle account passwords, email passwords, cookies, and local account databases.
remediation.suggestion: Add secure storage guidance for accounts.db, cookies, and exports, including file permissions and secret manager usage.

remediation.issue: Proxy examples may encourage unaudited proxy use for scraping.
remediation.suggestion: Label proxy values as placeholders and warn users to avoid untrusted proxies and credential exposure.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md lacks valid frontmatter for automated metadata scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Add valid YAML frontmatter with name, description, and supported tools so scanners can parse the skill reliably.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is a documentation example using proxy.example.com as a placeholder proxy URL. It does not execute network access or direct traffic to a real endpoint.
The IP address is 127.0.0.1 in a proxy configuration example. It is localhost documentation, not a hardcoded external destination.
The SOCKS proxy string is an illustrative local proxy setting in documentation. The broader proxy and scraping behavior is covered as a semantic risk rather than this line being malicious code.
The file write exports collected data to a caller-supplied output file in an example workflow. It is visible user-directed output, not hidden persistence or unauthorized file modification.
The results.json write is part of an explicit export example. There is no evidence of stealthy writes, path traversal, or overwriting protected files.
The example creates a local SQLite database for twscrape state while the same workflow adds accounts and cookies. This database can contain sensitive account or session material if copied directly.
The condition compares a tweet identifier to a target tweet identifier inside a search loop. It is not system reconnaissance or host inspection.
The numeric comparison is used to stop iterating through tweet results. It does not enumerate local system information or perform reconnaissance.
The URL is an upstream GitHub installation command for the development version. It is transparent package installation guidance, not hidden outbound communication.
The documentation states that twscrape creates accounts.db by default. Because twscrape manages account sessions, this local database may store sensitive account state.
The custom database path example directs users to persist twscrape account data in SQLite. This is legitimate use but still a sensitive local storage concern.
The CLI database option controls where account state is stored. Users need safeguards because the database can contain account and session information.

content.value_statement: Twitter/X data collection is hard to organize at scale. This skill guides twscrape setup, account management, searches, exports, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains installing twscrape from PyPI or the upstream GitHub repository.
Shows async searches, user lookups, tweet details, replies, followers, and trends.
Documents account setup with credentials, cookies, login, relogin, and status commands.
Shows proxy configuration through API parameters, environment variables, and per-account settings.
Provides JSON export and complete workflow examples for tweet and user data.
limitations: Requires valid Twitter/X accounts and network access.
Does not provide official Twitter/X API authorization or compliance review.
May encounter platform rate limits, account challenges, or suspended accounts.
Examples may store credentials, cookies, and scraped data on local disk unless secured.

use_cases.title: Monitor Public Topics
use_cases.description: Track public posts for keywords, trends, and account activity using async twscrape examples.

use_cases.title: Collect Research Samples
use_cases.description: Build repeatable workflows for public tweet searches, user timelines, and export files.

use_cases.title: Prototype Social Data Tools
use_cases.description: Use Python and CLI patterns to test social media analytics features before production design.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twscrape skill to show a minimal async Python example that searches Twitter/X for [query] and prints tweet text.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Accounts Securely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twscrape skill to explain account setup with cookies, accounts.db storage, and safe local handling for [project].

prompt_templates.title: Export User Activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twscrape skill to create a workflow that collects public posts for [username] and exports selected fields for analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scaled Collection Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twscrape skill to plan an ethical collection pipeline for [topic], including limits, storage, proxy choices, and compliance checks.

output_examples.input: Search for recent posts about Python and summarize the setup.
output_examples.output: A concise plan lists package setup, account login, async search, rate-limit notes, and a short result summary.

output_examples.input: Export a public user timeline for analysis.
output_examples.output: The response outlines username lookup, tweet collection limits, export fields, and cautions for local file storage.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot why no data is returned.
output_examples.output: A checklist covers account status, login state, query syntax, rate limits, and network or proxy settings.

best_practices: Use only accounts and data you are authorized to access.
Store accounts.db, cookies, and exports in protected locations with strict file permissions.
Set clear limits, logging, and retry rules before running long collection jobs.
anti_patterns: Using account rotation to evade platform controls or collect data without authorization.
Committing accounts.db, cookies, proxy credentials, or exports to source control.
Running high-volume collection without rate-limit, privacy, or legal review.

faq.question: Does this use the official Twitter/X API?
faq.answer: No. It guides twscrape workflows that use GraphQL-based scraping and account sessions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for prompts, Python examples, CLI commands, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it require Twitter/X accounts?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require valid accounts, login state, and network access.

faq.question: Where is account state stored?
faq.answer: twscrape uses accounts.db by default, or a custom SQLite database path you choose.

faq.question: Can it export data for analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show converting models to dictionaries and exporting selected data to files.

faq.question: What should I secure first?
faq.answer: Protect cookies, passwords, accounts.db, proxy credentials, and exported datasets from unauthorized access.
